Enum CommandParameterType

Namespace
OnixRuntime.Api.OnixClient.Commands
Assembly
OnixRuntime.dll

The various types of command parameters that can be parsed.

public enum CommandParameterType

Fields

Angles = 14

A pair of angles, yaw and pitch. Yaw is left-right and pitch is up-down. Angles.

Angles3 = 15

A triplet of angles, yaw and pitch and roll. Yaw is left-right and pitch is up-down and roll well, you flip it around.. Angles3.

Block = 16

A Block that is registered in this session.

BlockPos = 11

A single integer block position, supports relative (~). BlockPos.

Bool = 1

Just true or false, it's not that deep...

CommandPath = 0

This is used for sub commands, it's kind of like an enum but just one option will work.

Entities = 9

Targets multiple entities with a selector. Entity.

Entity = 8

This is any entity, it must be loaded for it to resolve. This is not too useful because it can be quite annoying to target a single entity. Entity.

EntitySelector = 10

This is a selector that can target entities, players, the command source (self) and more. It supports most selector options. CommandEntitySelector.

Enum = 20

This forces the user to chose between a few options. All you have to do is define your enum and have it in your commmand overload as a parameter. If you want to add icons or change the text that shows up in the auto-complete, you can use CommandEnumNameAttribute and CommandEnumIconAttribute on the enum members.

Float = 3

Any floating point number, like 0.5 or -3.14

Int = 2

Any number from int.MinValue to int.MaxValue

Item = 17

An Item that is registered in this session.

ItemStack = 18

An ItemStack without a count but having data and optional NBT data. Format: item,data{NBT} where only item is required. If you want count, add an int for it after the item, then you can just set Count.

Nbt = 19

This parses nbt text into an ObjectTag or an ArrayListTag. It must start with a { and end with a } or a [ and a ]. If you want to support both, make your parameter an NbtTag and check which you got!

Player = 6

This is a player entity, it must be loaded for it to resolve. Don't use this just for a name. Player.

Players = 7

This is a list of player entities, this lets the user select multiple players with selectors. Player.

Position = 12

A single floating-point position, supports relative (~). Vec3.

RawString = 5

This will dump everything remaining in the command as a single string, it does not support escape sequences or quotes. You can use the OnixCommandBase.RawStringAttribute on a string parameter to turn it into a raw string.

SoftEnum = 21

This gives suggestions to the user in the auto complete without enforcing. You can still have icons. This one you must register and maintain elsewhere in your code using. CommandEnumRegistry's RegisterSoftEnum methods.

String = 4

Some text, can be multiple words if quoted with "", it supports escape sequences like \n, \t, \r and "

Vec2 = 13

X and Y coordinates. Does not support lcoal or relative as it wouldn't know relative to what. Vec2.
